intro.title: Conditional Rendering with Ternary
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that displays a personalized greeting message based on a user's login status. You will learn how to use the ternary operator (? :) to conditionally render different UI elements directly within your JSX. This involves using TypeScript to define a boolean state variable that tracks whether a user is logged in. By the end, you'll understand how to implement clean, inline conditional logic to show or hide content in your React applications.
intro.usecase: Conditional rendering with ternary operators is essential for creating dynamic interfaces that respond to user state. In e-commerce sites, you'll see this pattern when showing 'Add to Cart' vs. 'Out of Stock' buttons based on inventory. Dashboard applications use it to toggle between 'Edit' and 'Save' modes in data tables, or to display loading spinners while fetching data. Form validations frequently employ ternaries to show error messages only when input fails checks, keeping interfaces clean until needed.
